subject: SET statement
notes: kb/Work PB458. 'Data-name-3 shall reference a dynamic-length elementary data item' - the explicit arm always enforced it (COBOL1568) and the bare arm now resolves the receiver through the SAME ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving instead of a private peek. The peek's first line refused any receiver carrying a dataReferenceSuffix, a guard aimed at subscripts; a suffix also carries QUALIFICATION, so SET D OF G TO 2 - legal source under 8.4.2.2.3 rule 2 - fell through to the Format-1 numeric store and terminated on a raw runtime exception, while SET SIZE OF D OF G TO 2 worked. 13.16.3 SR18 leaves an OCCURS clause impossible on a DYNAMIC LENGTH entry, so the subscript half of the guard had nothing legal to exclude and the qualification half was pure loss. MEASURED: SET D OF G TO 2 now prints D=[AB] L=2, identical to the explicit arm.
